quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Left turns are not allowed here.
You can turn left only after you stop.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turns are not allowed here.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means left turns are prohibited.

questions.question: A bad suspension system can cause:
questions.explanation: The suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives you a smooth ride. If your car bounces too much after hitting a bump or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: If dust or smoke makes it hard to see other vehicles, you should slow down and turn on your:
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly. Other drivers also need to see you.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person has moved far away from your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person has moved far away from your path.
questions.explanation: When a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog crosses the street, you must stop. Stay stopped until they are far away from your vehicle. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: To pass safely on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check how far away any oncoming vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away any oncoming vehicles are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are going. They may be faster than they look. Only pass when you are sure you have enough room to change lanes safely. If you are not certain about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait to pass.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, you should:

options.text: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
questions.explanation: Always wear both parts of a two-part seat belt system. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection. Even if you have an automatic shoulder belt, you must also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: Which statement about work zones is true?

options.text: Fines in work zones are the same as regular traffic violations.
You must slow down in work zones.
Slow down only if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down in work zones.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed in work zones and be ready to stop for equipment. Driving slowly through work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and road workers safe.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when a traffic light turns yellow. You should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed through the intersection without looking out.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross the intersection with caution.

questions.question: Roads are most slippery:

options.text: After heavy rain for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.

questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. Water mixes with oil and dirt on the road, making it very slippery. Be extra careful when driving on wet roads.

questions.question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: No one can pass from either direction.
Everyone can pass from both directions.
Only drivers next to the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only drivers next to the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line and a dashed yellow line, only drivers next to the dashed line can cross the center line to pass. Drivers next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. If one yellow line is solid and one is broken, drivers on the solid line side cannot pass. If both lines are solid, no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: At an intersection with stop signs on all corners, yield the right-of-way to any driver:
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: To improve visibility lowered by rain or fog, drivers should use their:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off water and precipitation, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When driving in fog or mist, never put your headlights on the high beam setting because:

options.text: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
Approaching vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: High beams in fog reflect back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should be driving:

options.text: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
More slowly than the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Match the freeway traffic speed when merging, unless traffic is going over the speed limit.

questions.question: This yellow warning sign means:

options.text: You are approaching a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive with caution, and watch for children.

questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers near schools to slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when following another car. High beams only work in rural areas with no other vehicles nearby.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: Always look left and right at intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings to check for traffic or pedestrians.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating your vehicle.
You should always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply brakes gently with increasing pressure to stop smoothly.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow traffic light. If you have not already entered the intersection, you should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.

questions.explanation: When you see a yellow light and have not entered the intersection, stop safely. Only proceed through if you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: Which of these is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.

questions.explanation: Look at the road and check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to stay aware of hazards. Staring only ahead is dangerous. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is retracted and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is retracted and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, you must stop completely. Stay stopped until the lights turn off, the stop arm goes in, and the bus moves.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on a thin layer of water instead of the road. To prevent hydroplaning in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep the same speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet pavement. Slow down when the road is wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unsafe to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unsafe to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your ability to drive. They are especially dangerous when combined with alcohol.

questions.question: The speed limit in school zones is:
questions.explanation: Unless marked otherwise, do not drive faster than 20 mph in school zones. Always be careful when driving near children.

questions.question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:
questions.explanation: Traffic lights control traffic and prevent crashes. Follow traffic signals unless a police officer is directing traffic instead.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Last turn before a toll road.

questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barrels mean a work zone. Stay alert and be ready for unexpected conditions. This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. Obey the flagger's directions.

questions.question: If you come to an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and look both ways. Cross the intersection carefully and watch for other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: In traffic moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most vehicles.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most vehicles.

questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic (as long as it is within the speed limit). Vehicles traveling at the same speed in the same direction cannot crash into each other. Crashes happen when vehicles drive at different speeds.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic going straight. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: How do sudden wind gusts affect driving on highways?

options.text: They can affect all types of vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can affect all types of vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind can cause problems for all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dust and dirt, and it can also push vehicles sideways.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, reduce your speed and stay alert. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers and sudden changes.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When you feel tired, drive to the nearest rest stop to take a nap, stretch, or change drivers. Caffeine pills are not a safe substitute for rest.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Turn in that direction after checking for traffic.
Do not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
Turn in that direction after stopping completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must wait until the light turns green or a green arrow appears before turning.

questions.question: When should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to see traffic behind you.
To check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors frequently while driving. This helps you know where nearby vehicles are at all times.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance or acceleration ramp, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the highway.
questions.explanation: When entering a highway, yield to traffic already on it. Merge safely when there is a gap in traffic.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Brake as hard as you can.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, ease off the gas or brake to regain balance. Steer in the direction of the skid to get control back.

questions.question: You have a green light, but pedestrians are crossing. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians in the intersection. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does a yellow pennant-shaped sign tell you?
questions.explanation: A yellow pennant-shaped sign marks a no passing zone.

questions.question: What does a yellow left arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending.

questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means two things. First, you must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic. Second, the protected left turn is about to end.

questions.question: How can you help the driver behind you stay at a safe distance?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.

questions.explanation: Maintain a steady speed to help the driver behind you keep a safe distance. Also signal your turns, lane changes, and when you slow down.

questions.question: When bad weather or darkness requires lights while driving, use:
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a pedestrian crosswalk is ahead.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic may be merging into your lane ahead.

questions.question: Who must wear a safety belt in a moving vehicle?
questions.explanation: All people in a moving vehicle must wear safety belts by law. The driver is responsible for making sure this happens. Children must use proper child-restraint systems.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and hazmat trucks.
Watch for trains coming from either direction.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings slowly and carefully. Only cross when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles like school buses and hazmat trucks, which must stop at all railroad crossings.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In any crosswalk at an intersection.

questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians crossing at any marked or unmarked crosswalk. For safety, always yield to people crossing any street.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: On the left side of the cab.
On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have much larger blind spots than cars. The driver cannot see vehicles behind or to the left side of the truck. If you cannot see the driver's face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: On a road with a single broken white centerline, you:

options.text: May cross the line to change lanes.
May change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: May cross the line to change lanes.
questions.explanation: A broken white line means traffic in both lanes travels the same direction. You may cross it to pass or change lanes when it is safe to do so.
